changed_views: Update the October 24 Mistral preview: public Large 4 weights are now released; the specialized partner variant has a separate access policy.

Agent cost comparisons should include context replay after cache expiry. A small user message can accompany substantial input processing; this episode supplies an operator anecdote, not a measured savings estimate.
Kepler presents a potential manufacturing route through older-node capacity. Treat the technical rationale and production targets separately from demonstrated commercial performance.
follow_ups: For an actual agent workload, compare audited action and completion failures across models while controlling for task mix, conversation length, and judging error.
Inspect cache-hit rates, expired-cache input charges, completed-task quality, and latency before accepting a router savings claim.
Track Kepler sample availability and independently documented memory density, endurance, yield, power, and customer qualification against its production schedule.
Evaluate the released Mistral weights on relevant workloads and deployment costs; keep public-model results separate from any vetted-partner variant.

signals.claim: Arena’s alignment index evaluates observable failures in agent sessions: unauthorized actions, false attribution of user intent, and false claims that work was completed.
signals.evidence: Angelopoulos describes checking user guardrails and agent traces against reported actions, and argues for measurement during real work. Arena’s [primary methodology article](https://arena.ai/blog/ai-alignment-index) documents rubric-based judging with human review and conversation-length adjustment. This supports a specific measurement approach, not a conclusion about a model’s internal motives or its safety in every deployment. The article predates this compilation, and the interview’s rankings should be read as a dated platform snapshot.

signals.claim: Arena reports expensive follow-up turns after long agent sessions outlive their cache, motivating routing and cache management alongside model selection.
signals.evidence: At 12:53, Angelopoulos says internal traces showed approximately $40 charges when users returned the next day to a long conversation and sent a brief acknowledgement after its cache had expired. He presents this as a reason for Arena’s MAX router and more deliberate caching. This is an operator’s anecdote; no bill, model configuration, context size, or controlled cost comparison is supplied. The mechanism is relevant to agent economics, but the quoted cost is not a general price and does not demonstrate MAX savings.

signals.claim: Kepler proposes denser ferroelectric memory and closer memory-compute integration as a way to improve inference while using older-node fabrication capacity.
signals.evidence: Debo Olaosebikan, identified by the segment introduction despite erroneous speaker labels, describes replacing a six-transistor SRAM cell with a transistor-plus-ferroelectric-capacitor structure and pursuing vertical density. At 20:42 he argues that older-node fabs could manufacture useful memory products without depending on leading-edge lithography. Kepler’s [primary description](https://keplercompute.com/act-one) supports the architecture direction. Its [published schedule](https://keplercompute.com/) targets sampling by year-end and production in 2027. Those are company plans, not proof of volume readiness, yield, endurance, delivered cost, or superiority over advanced-node alternatives.

signals.claim: Mistral Large 4 has moved from the prior digest’s preview to a public open-weight release, while a specialized cyber variant remains a separate vetted-partner offering.
signals.evidence: The introduction describes the new weight release, and Sagar Vaze distinguishes the released model’s safeguards from access for trusted partners. Mistral’s [release announcement](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/) confirms public weights and a preview of the specialized variant with enterprise vetting and contractual restrictions. Hugging Face’s [October 29 release article](https://huggingface.co/blog/mistral-large4) confirms FP8 and NVFP4 availability under the custom Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License. This changes availability relative to October 24; it does not establish unrestricted access to the specialized variant or independently validate the vendor’s benchmark and safety claims.

summary: This AI:AM compilation connects agent reliability and operating costs with changes in memory hardware and model availability. Anastasios Angelopoulos describes production-trace evaluation and expensive cache expiry; Debo Olaosebikan outlines Kepler’s older-fab memory strategy; Sagar Vaze distinguishes Mistral’s released public weights from its vetted-partner cyber offering. Source coverage combines the full publisher transcript with official video captions, including the omitted opening montage and closing credits. Timestamps below use publisher-transcript time, approximately 6:34 behind video time. The video runs 1:26:42 versus RSS 1:27:57; the remaining 75-second difference is unverified. Segment introductions correct erroneous automatic speaker labels. Host transitions use disclosed cloned narration.
why_it_matters: The useful changes are concrete: evaluate agents through observable failures in actual work; account for expired context caches in operating costs; assess memory innovation against manufacturing evidence; and distinguish Mistral’s released public weights from its separately vetted variant. The release updates the October 24 digest’s preview status. None of the excerpts establishes a general alignment guarantee, measured router savings, or commercially qualified Kepler performance.
